originalTitle: South Africa dump site collapse kills 14 suspected illegal miners
title: A Sad Story from South Africa: When a Big Dirt Hill Fell Down
content:
Hello Friends! Sad News from South Africa

Hello everyone! Your kid-friendly reporter from Africa is here today with some very important, but a little bit sad, news from a country called South Africa. South Africa is a beautiful country far, far away, in the southern part of our amazing continent, Africa. Something very serious happened there recently, and we want to talk about it in a way that helps us understand and also think about safety. A big pile of dirt and rocks, like a huge hill, suddenly fell down. This happened in a place where people sometimes go to look for special things hidden in the ground. It was a very scary moment for many people, and it made a lot of us feel sad.

What is a Dump Site?

The place where this big hill fell down is called a "dump site." Now, what exactly is a dump site in this story? Imagine people digging deep into the earth to find shiny rocks like gold or diamonds. When they dig, they bring out lots and lots of earth, dirt, and smaller rocks that they don't need. They pile all this extra stuff up. Over many, many years, these piles grow super big, like giant mountains of old dirt and leftover rocks. These are the dump sites. They might look like ordinary hills, but they are not always strong. Sometimes, they can become wobbly, just like a sandcastle that hasn't been built very well. And if they get too wobbly, they can suddenly fall down, very quickly! This is what happened in South Africa. **Did you know?** South Africa is famous all over the world for its gold! People have been digging for gold there for hundreds of years. Gold is a shiny, yellow metal that people use to make beautiful jewelry and other special things.

Who Were the People There?

The people who were at this dump site are sometimes called "miners." Miners are people who dig deep into the earth to find valuable rocks or minerals. But in this sad story, the people were called "suspected illegal miners." What does "illegal" mean? It means they were digging in a place where they were not allowed to be. They didn't have the right papers or the right safety equipment. It's like playing in a dangerous area where grown-ups have told you not to go. When people mine illegally, they often don't have strong tunnels to work in, or special helmets, or doctors nearby if something goes wrong. This makes it very, very dangerous for them. These people were likely looking for small pieces of gold or other valuable things left behind in the old dirt piles. They often do this because they need money to take care of their families, but it's a very risky way to earn a living.

What Happened When the Hill Fell?

When the big dirt hill fell down, it was a sudden and terrible noise. Lots of earth, rocks, and dust came tumbling down all at once. Imagine a giant wall of mud and stones moving very, very fast. People who were near or under it got caught. They couldn't run away in time. The heavy dirt and rocks trapped them. It is very, very sad to say that some of these people got hurt badly. And even more sadly, 14 people lost their lives. This means they are no longer with us. It's a very difficult and sad thing to think about, and it makes us feel very sorry for their families and friends. We send our biggest hugs to everyone in South Africa who is feeling sad right now.

Brave Helpers Are Looking

Even though it's a very sad situation, there are brave people working hard to help. These brave people are called "rescuers" and they work with the "authorities" (these are the grown-ups who help manage things, like the police and special rescue teams). They are trying their best to find anyone who might still be trapped under all that fallen dirt and rocks. They use special tools and even their own hands to dig carefully through the rubble. "Rubble" means all the broken pieces of dirt and rocks. They work day and night, hoping to find more people and to help them. They are heroes, trying to make sure no one is left behind. They want to help everyone they can.

Why Are These Places Dangerous?

We've learned that these dump sites are not safe places. The ground can be tricky. It's not like the solid ground we walk on every day. These hills of waste earth can be unstable, which means they can move or fall without any warning. They might look strong, but they can be very weak inside. Also, as we talked about, doing any kind of mining without the right safety gear and permission is super dangerous. Good, legal mines have strong support beams in their tunnels, special air to breathe, and doctors ready to help. Illegal mining has none of this, which makes it a very, very risky job. **Did you know?** When miners work in safe, legal mines, they wear bright helmets with lights, strong boots, and special suits to protect them. They also have engineers who make sure the tunnels are strong and won't fall down!

Learning from Sad Events

When sad things like this happen, it's important for us to learn from them. The most important lesson is always about safety. We must always listen to the grown-ups who tell us where it's safe to play and where it's not. We must also understand that working in dangerous places without proper safety measures can have very sad outcomes. The government and many good people in South Africa want everyone to be safe. They are trying to find better ways for people to earn money so they don't have to go to such dangerous places. Our continent, Africa, is a place of many hopes and dreams, and we all want our people to be safe and happy.

Sending Our Love to South Africa

We send our deepest care and thoughts to all the families who lost someone in this sad event in South Africa. We also cheer for the brave rescuers who are still working hard. Let's all remember to be safe, listen to important rules, and always care for one another. **Did you know?** Africa is the second-largest continent in the world! It has 54 amazing countries, each with its own special stories and kind people. We are all connected, and when one part of Africa hurts, we all feel it. Stay safe, everyone!
summary: In South Africa, a big pile of old mining dirt called a dump site fell down, sadly trapping people and killing 14 who were looking for valuable rocks without safety or permission, while brave rescuers are still searching for anyone else caught under the rubble.
whyMatters: This story matters because it shows us how important safety is and why we should never go to dangerous places, especially when grown-ups say it's not safe, and it reminds us to be kind and sad for the people who got hurt and their families.

originalTitle: Ethiopia drone strike in north kills three, Tigray sources say
title: Let's Keep Schools Safe! News from Ethiopia
content:
Hello, Super Stars of Africa!

Hello, my wonderful friends! It's your Reporter Pendo here, bringing you news from across our amazing continent, Africa. I hope you are all smiling and ready to learn something new today. Today, we have a story from a country called Ethiopia. Ethiopia is a beautiful country right here in Africa, full of history and wonderful people. Sometimes, things happen that make us a little sad, but it's important to talk about them and hope for good things.

Something Happened Near a School

Not long ago, something happened near a school in Ethiopia. A school is a very special place, isn't it? It's where you go to learn new things, read exciting books, draw colorful pictures, and play with your friends. Schools should always be safe places for children like you. This happened when the school was on a holiday. Do you remember when your school has holidays? It's a time to rest, play, and spend time with your family. So, no children were in the school building at that moment, which is a good thing. But a flying machine made a big noise near the school. This flying machine is sometimes called a 'drone.' It's like a small robot that can fly high up in the sky. Grown-ups use drones for many different things. Sometimes, people use drones to take pictures or videos from high up, like a bird. Other times, they can be used to carry things or to check on farms. But in this story, the drone caused a problem near the school. When something like this happens, it makes everyone feel a bit worried. We want all schools, everywhere in the world, to be peaceful and safe places for every child.

Where is Ethiopia?

Did you know that Africa is a very big continent? It has many, many countries, each with its own special stories and people. Ethiopia is one of those fantastic countries. It's in the eastern part of Africa, far away from some countries and closer to others. Imagine looking at a big map of Africa. You would find Ethiopia there, looking like a big, beautiful puzzle piece. The people of Ethiopia are known for their friendly smiles and delicious food. They have ancient churches carved into rocks and famous long-distance runners! It's a land of many wonders. Did you know? Ethiopia is one of the oldest countries in the world! It has a very, very long history, older than most countries you know.

Why Are Schools So Important?

Think about your school for a moment. What do you love about it? Is it your teacher who teaches you new words? Or maybe it's playing football with your friends during break time? Schools are like a second home. They are where you grow your brain, learn to share, and discover new talents. Every morning, children all over Africa wake up excited to go to school. They learn to read stories, solve number puzzles, and even sing beautiful songs. This helps them grow up to be smart and kind adults who can help their communities. When a school is hurt or affected, it makes us sad because it means a safe place for learning has been touched by something difficult. We want to protect these special places. Did you know? There are more than 1.5 billion children who go to school all around the world! That's a huge number of learners, just like you!

What is a Drone? Let's Learn!

Remember we talked about the flying machine, the 'drone'? Let's learn a little more about it. Imagine a toy airplane, but a bit bigger and controlled by someone from the ground, or even from far away. Drones don't have pilots sitting inside them like a big airplane does. They fly by themselves or are guided by a person using a special remote control. They have propellers that spin very fast to lift them into the air. Some drones are as small as your hand, and some are as big as a small car! They can fly very high and see things that people on the ground cannot see easily. It's like having eyes in the sky! Usually, drones are used for good things. Farmers might use them to check their crops. Rescue teams might use them to look for people who are lost. Sometimes, photographers use them to take amazing pictures of landscapes. But sometimes, like in this sad story, drones can be used in ways that are not good. We hope that everyone uses these flying machines for peace and helpfulness. Did you know? The very first flying machines were kites, flown many, many years ago in China! People loved to see things fly even back then.

Hoping for Peace and Safety

When things like this happen, it reminds us how important peace is. Peace means everyone is safe, happy, and can go about their day without fear. It means children can go to school and play without worrying. Our hearts are with the people in Ethiopia, especially the children and their families. We hope that the grown-ups who are in charge will work very hard to make sure everyone is safe. It's important for all of us to remember that we can help by being kind to each other and by wishing for peace in every corner of Africa and the world. Every little wish for peace can make a difference. We want all schools to be places of joy and learning, not places where bad things happen. This is a big job for grown-ups to make sure of this. Let's all hope for a future where every child in Ethiopia, and everywhere else, can go to school feeling completely safe and happy, learning and playing all day long. Thank you for listening, my smart friends! Remember to always be kind, be curious, and keep shining bright! This is Reporter Pendo, signing off with a big wish for peace for all of us. Bye for now!
summary: Reporter Pendo tells us about a school in Ethiopia where something sad happened with a flying machine, and why it's important for all schools to be safe places for children.
whyMatters: It's important because schools are special places where children learn and play, and every child deserves to feel safe and happy at school.

originalTitle: A burial row over Zambia's late president has turned its election into a hot contest
title: A Big Goodbye, a Little Disagreement, and a New Election in Zambia!
content:
Hello from Sunny Zambia!

Hello, amazing friends! We are here in beautiful Zambia, a wonderful country right in the middle of Africa. Zambia is famous for its friendly people, its amazing animals like elephants and giraffes, and its stunning waterfalls! Imagine your school. You have a head teacher who helps everyone, makes sure rules are followed, and looks after all the students and teachers. Well, a country also has a special leader! Our country, Zambia, has a leader who helps everyone in the whole country. They are like the head teacher for Zambia! This leader is called the President. The President helps make sure our roads are good, our schools are working, and that everyone has food and feels safe. It's a very big and important job! Our current President is Mr. Hakainde Hichilema. He works very hard for all of us.

What is a President?

A President is the most important helper for a whole country. They live in a special house, often called State House, and they travel around to meet people and see how things are going. They talk to other leaders from different countries too! Think about a big football team. The President is like the captain of the team, guiding everyone to work together. They make sure important decisions are made carefully, so that our country can grow strong and happy. It's a job that needs a lot of listening and thinking! **Did you know?** The President of Zambia also helps protect our wonderful national parks and all the incredible animals that live there!

Choosing Our Leaders: Elections!

How do we choose this very important person, the President? We have something super important called an election! An election is like a big voting day for the whole country. On election day, grown-ups go to special places to put a secret paper into a box. This paper has the names of people who want to be President. By choosing a name, they are saying who they think will be the best leader for Zambia. It’s a very fair way to choose! Our President, Mr. Hakainde Hichilema, was chosen by the people of Zambia in the last election. Now, it will soon be time for another election. This means people will get to choose again if they want Mr. Hichilema to continue leading them, or if they want someone new. Every vote counts! It's how everyone in the country gets to have a say in who helps guide Zambia into the future. It’s like when your class votes for who gets to be the line leader for the week. Everyone's choice matters!

When an Important Person Leaves Us

Sometimes, very important people who have helped our country for a long time pass away. This means they are no longer with us. It's a very sad time for everyone, especially their family and friends, and the whole country feels sad too. Not long ago, a past President of Zambia, Mr. Edgar Lungu, sadly passed away. He was a leader for our country before Mr. Hichilema. When someone who was once President passes away, it is a very big event. People want to show great respect and say a special goodbye to them. This special goodbye is called a burial. A burial is when we lay someone to rest, usually in a special place, and remember all the good things they did. It’s a time for mourning, which means feeling sad, but also a time for remembering and honouring their life and what they did for Zambia. Everyone wants to make sure this goodbye is done in a way that truly shows how much the person was valued.

A Disagreement About Saying Goodbye

Now, here is something a little bit tricky. Sometimes, even when everyone wants to show respect and say a good goodbye, there can be disagreements. Imagine you and your best friend want to play two different games. You both want to have fun, but you can't agree on which game to play first! Something like this has happened with the goodbye for our past President, Mr. Edgar Lungu. There has been a 'burial row.' This means there is a disagreement about how and where his burial should happen. Some people, perhaps his family, might have one idea, and other people, like the government, might have another idea. Everyone means well, and everyone wants to honour Mr. Lungu. But when there are different ideas, it can make people feel sad, confused, or even a little bit upset. It's a very important discussion because it's about showing respect to a person who once led our whole country. **Did you know?** Many countries have special national cemeteries where past leaders and heroes are buried with great honour.

Why Does This Matter for Our Country?

You might be thinking, 'Why is a disagreement about a goodbye so important for the whole country and the election?' Well, it's because people watch very closely how our current leaders handle big and sensitive things like this. When there is a disagreement about how to say goodbye to a past leader, people in Zambia pay attention. They want to see if the current President, Mr. Hakainde Hichilema, and his government, are handling it with kindness, fairness, and respect for everyone. If people feel that the situation is not handled well, it can make them feel unhappy. And these feelings can sometimes make them think differently about who they want to vote for in the upcoming election. They might wonder if the current leaders are truly listening to everyone and showing respect to all parts of the country. It’s like if your class monitor wasn’t being fair to all the students; you might think about choosing someone else next time. It's about trust and how leaders show they care for everyone, even for those who are no longer with us or who have different ideas. **Did you know?** When leaders handle disagreements peacefully, it helps make the whole country stronger and happier!

Showing Respect to Everyone

One of the most important things in life is to show respect. This means treating everyone with kindness and understanding, even if you don't always agree with them. When someone important like a President passes away, showing respect is extra important. It helps our country to stay united, like a big, happy family. Even with disagreements about goodbyes, everyone wants Zambia to be peaceful and to move forward. Working together, even when it's tough, makes us all stronger. When we show respect, we remember that we are all Zambian. We all want the best for our country. By being understanding and kind, we can help heal any sadness and bring everyone closer.

Looking Ahead for Zambia

So, as the next election gets closer, people in Zambia will be thinking about many things. They will think about how the country is run, how disagreements are solved, and how everyone is treated. The way the goodbye to Mr. Edgar Lungu is handled will be one of the things people remember. Everyone hopes that Zambia will continue to be a country where people can choose their leaders fairly, and where everyone treats each other with respect and kindness. We all want a bright and happy future for Zambia! Let’s keep hoping for peace and unity in our beautiful country. That way, our leaders, whoever they may be, can keep working hard to make Zambia an even better place for all of us, especially for all the children!
summary: People in Zambia are getting ready to choose their leader again, but there's a disagreement about how to say goodbye to a past president, which is making everyone talk about who they will vote for.
whyMatters: It's important because how people say goodbye to someone special can make a big difference in how they feel about their leaders and who they want to guide their country next.
